## 1. Sleep Hygiene (General Behavioral and Environmental Factors)

<sub>ICD-11 (unverified): 7A60 Circadian rhythm sleep-wake disorder, delayed sleep phase type, 7A61 Circadian rhythm sleep-wake disorder, advanced sleep phase type</sub>

### 2.1 Light Exposure and Circadian Rhythm Regulation

<sub>ICD-11 (unverified): 7A6Z Circadian rhythm sleep-wake disorders, unspecified</sub>

- **2.1.1 Get outside in daylight soon after you wake up.**

- **2.1.2 Use dimmer, warmer lights in the evening.**  
  <sub>`less-bright-light-in-the-evening` · source: “Reduce blue light exposure in the evening” · R4 Ea3 I4 N3! Ev5 · 1 cited</sub>
- **2.1.3 If you need light at night, use a dim red or amber one.**  
  <sub>`use-dim-red-light-at-night` · source: “Use dim red light at night instead of blue or white light – Red light has the least impact on melatonin production and circadian rhythm.” · R2 Ea3 I4! N4 Ev4! · no citations · for: parents-and-caregivers</sub>
- **2.1.4 Turn the lights down little by little as bedtime gets closer.**  
  <sub>`dim-lights-gradually` · source: “Use smart lighting to gradually dim before bed” · R– Ea– I– N– Ev– · no citations</sub>
- **2.1.5 Some people wear blue-light-blocking glasses in the evening.**

  <sub>`late-afternoon-daylight` · source: “Late-Afternoon Sunlight Viewing” · R– Ea– I– N– Ev– · no citations</sub>
- **＋ Your body is coldest a couple of hours before you usually wake.**

- **＋ After dark, keep indoor lights low and screens dim.**  
  <sub>`dim-the-lights-after-dark` · source: “Dim the Lights at Night” · R– Ea– I– N– Ev– · no citations</sub>

## Myths

- **Alcohol may make you drowsy, but it makes sleep worse later in the night.**  
  <sub>`myth-alcohol-helps-sleep` · “Myth: Alcohol helps you sleep better.” · 5 cited · for: adults</sub>
- **Sleeping in on weekends doesn't fully make up for short sleep during the week.**  
  <sub>`myth-weekend-catch-up` · “Myth: You can "catch up" on lost sleep during weekends.” · 3 cited</sub>
- **Regular exercise helps sleep, but hard workouts right before bed can keep you up.**  
  <sub>`myth-exercise-right-before-bed` · “Myth: Exercising right before bed improves sleep.” · 4 cited</sub>
- **Falling asleep to TV can make sleep lighter and more broken.**  
  <sub>`myth-tv-helps-you-sleep` · “Myth: Watching TV helps you fall asleep.” · 4 cited</sub>
- **Loud, frequent snoring can be a sign of sleep apnea and is worth checking.**  
  <sub>`myth-snoring-is-harmless` · “Myth: Snoring is harmless.” · 8 cited · for: people-who-snore-or-may-have-sleep-apnea</sub>
